messages.content: Rework Houston around the Thursday morning flight and only one hotel night. Compare the downtown Hilton with the hotel near the site, including every local transportation cost. Nothing should be booked.

I’ll use the selected Thursday nonstop from ORD at 7:05 a.m., arriving IAH at 9:48 a.m., and the Friday nonstop at 7:10 p.m., arriving ORD at 9:54 p.m. Airfare remains $486. The hotel candidates are Hilton Americas-Houston downtown and Embassy Suites by Hilton Houston Energy Corridor near the Friday site. Are you checking a bag, and what time does Thursday’s summit end?
Carry-on only. The summit starts at 1:30 and should end at 5:00. I need enough time to get from IAH to the Hilton, leave my bag, and be seated before it starts.

With a 9:48 a.m. arrival, allow 15 to 25 minutes to reach the rideshare pickup area. IAH to the Hilton is normally 35 to 55 minutes at that time. That puts you at the hotel around 10:38 to 11:08 a.m. Even allowing 15 minutes to leave the bag, you would be ready by about 11:23, more than two hours before the 1:30 start. The summit is inside the Hilton, so there is no separate transfer.
Good. Give me the full downtown version first, including Friday’s trip to the site and then IAH.

Hilton Americas is $249.00 for Thursday night plus $42.33 in taxes, totaling $291.33. Thursday’s IAH-to-Hilton rideshare is estimated at $46 to $68. On Friday, the Hilton to the site near I-10 and Beltway 8 should take 30 to 45 minutes and cost $38 to $55. Leaving at 8:00 a.m. gives you a likely arrival between 8:30 and 8:45 for the 9:00 site visit. After the 11:30 scheduled finish and manager wrap-up, the site-to-IAH ride should take 30 to 45 minutes and cost $42 to $60.
What departure time from the site are you using for the airport calculation? The wrap-up could run to 3:30.

Using a 3:45 p.m. departure, you should reach IAH between 4:15 and 4:30. That leaves 2 hours 40 minutes to 2 hours 55 minutes before the 7:10 flight. With carry-on only, that is a solid margin. The three downtown-plan rideshares total $126 at the low end and $183 at the high end.
And the complete downtown total?

The downtown plan totals $903.33 at the low transportation estimate or $960.33 at the high estimate: $486 airfare, $291.33 lodging, and $126 to $183 in rideshares. No parking charge applies if you use rideshares.
Now run the Embassy Suites version. I still have to attend the summit at the Hilton, so include both Thursday transfers.

Embassy Suites Houston Energy Corridor is $189.00 plus $32.13 tax, totaling $221.13 for Thursday night. You would rideshare from IAH to the Hilton for $46 to $68 and arrive around 10:38 to 11:08 a.m. After the summit ends at 5:00 p.m., Hilton to Embassy Suites is about 30 to 50 minutes in afternoon traffic and $36 to $52. Friday morning, Embassy Suites to the site is 10 to 15 minutes and $14 to $22; leaving at 8:25 gets you there around 8:35 to 8:40. The site-to-IAH leg remains 30 to 45 minutes and $42 to $60.
Total that one, and compare it directly with downtown.

The four rideshares for the near-site plan total $138 to $202. Including the $486 airfare and $221.13 hotel, the complete estimate is $845.13 to $909.13. At the high end it saves $51.20 versus downtown. The tradeoff is the extra Thursday evening transfer after a full summit day; Friday morning is roughly 20 to 30 minutes shorter.
Check a rental car too. Include the actual parking charges at both hotels and at the summit, not just the rental rate.

The compact rental from Thursday morning through Friday afternoon is $146.72 including estimated rental taxes and facility fees. Budget $25 for fuel and tolls. Hilton self-parking is $38 overnight. Embassy Suites parking is free, but if you stay there you would pay about $32 to park at the Hilton during the summit. Those figures do not include optional rental coverage.
How does driving affect the timing?

From IAH to the Hilton, driving is still about 35 to 55 minutes, plus roughly 10 to 15 minutes to reach the garage, park, and leave your bag. You would likely be settled by 11:20 a.m., preserving more than two hours before the summit. If you stay at Embassy Suites, the post-summit drive is the weak point: leaving downtown around 5:00 p.m. can take 45 to 65 minutes, versus the broader 30-to-50-minute rideshare estimate because you must retrieve the car and enter peak traffic. Friday’s hotel-to-site drive is 10 to 15 minutes, and site to IAH remains 30 to 45 minutes.
Give me both car totals. Also make sure the Hilton option does not accidentally include summit parking twice.

For the Hilton stay, the car plan is $987.05: $486 airfare, $291.33 hotel, $146.72 rental, $38 Hilton overnight self-parking, and $25 fuel and tolls. There is no separate summit parking charge because you are already parked at the hotel. For Embassy Suites, the car plan is $910.85: $486 airfare, $221.13 hotel, $146.72 rental, $32 Hilton summit parking, free Embassy Suites parking, and $25 fuel and tolls.
So the cheapest practical choice is Embassy Suites with rideshares, but it adds the transfer after the summit. Is there any timing problem Friday if I leave the site at 3:45?

No. From the site, both hotel choices converge on the same 30-to-45-minute route to IAH. A 3:45 p.m. departure should put you at the terminal around 4:15 to 4:30 for the 7:10 p.m. nonstop, leaving at least 2 hours 40 minutes. The Embassy Suites rideshare plan is the lowest high-end estimate at $909.13, narrowly below its $910.85 rental-car version and $51.20 below the downtown rideshare plan.

Use Embassy Suites and rideshares as the working combination. Recap the exact schedule, all route estimates, and the full one-night totals for both hotels so I can send it internally. Keep every component unbooked.

Working combination, entirely unbooked: Thursday nonstop ORD-IAH departs 7:05 a.m. and arrives 9:48 a.m.; airfare is $486. With carry-on only, reach the rideshare area around 10:03 to 10:13, then ride 35 to 55 minutes to Hilton Americas for $46 to $68. Expected arrival is 10:38 to 11:08, leaving more than two hours before the 1:30 p.m. summit. After the 5:00 p.m. finish, rideshare 30 to 50 minutes to Embassy Suites Houston Energy Corridor for $36 to $52. Its one-night total is $221.13, comprising $189.00 room and $32.13 tax. Friday, leave around 8:25 a.m.; the site is 10 to 15 minutes away and the ride is $14 to $22 for the 9:00 a.m. visit. If the wrap-up ends at 3:30, depart by 3:45; allow 30 to 45 minutes and $42 to $60 to IAH, arriving around 4:15 to 4:30 for the 7:10 p.m. nonstop to ORD, arriving 9:54 p.m. Embassy Suites rideshares total $138 to $202, making the complete trip $845.13 to $909.13. For comparison, Hilton Americas is $291.33 for one night, including $249.00 room and $42.33 tax. Its three rideshares total $126 to $183, and the complete trip is $903.33 to $960.33. Rental-car totals are $910.85 with Embassy Suites, including $32 summit parking and free hotel parking, or $987.05 with the Hilton, including $38 overnight self-parking and no separate summit charge. Flights, hotel, rideshares, and rental alternatives all remain unbooked and subject to availability and live pricing.
